key_insight: SpaceNum shows that numeric outputs from VLMs — both action-like transitions and absolute spatial coordinates — are not reliably grounded in visual perception; a unified benchmark exposes distinct failure modes across these two settings.
problem_solved: Clarifies whether numbers produced by VLMs reflect true spatial perception (grounded understanding) versus linguistic or dataset shortcuts, and provides a standardized way to evaluate numerical/spatial grounding.
method: Define two complementary settings: (a) numbers as dynamic transitions (action magnitudes/deltas) and (b) numbers as static spatial coordinates (absolute positions).
Build SpaceNum — a controlled benchmark with synthetic and real-scene probes, targeted perturbations, and task splits that isolate perceptual grounding from language priors.
Evaluate diverse VLMs with diagnostics and metrics (accuracy, calibration, generalization under perturbations) to identify systematic errors and model-specific failure modes.
impact: Provides practitioners a clear diagnostic and benchmarking tool to assess and improve VLMs for embodied tasks (navigation, manipulation) where correct numerical/spatial outputs are critical for safety and reliability.
visual_elements: Split-panel diagram showing the two settings: dynamic transitions (arrow/magnitude overlay) vs. static coordinates (point markers with x,y labels).
Example image with model-predicted numbers vs. ground-truth overlays to illustrate perceptual vs. spurious predictions.
Bar/line chart comparing error and calibration across models and across perturbation types (occlusion, viewpoint shift, scale).
Pipeline flowchart of the SpaceNum benchmark: dataset generation → task types → diagnostics → metrics and failure-mode mapping.
paper_title: SPACENUM: Revisiting Spatial Numerical Understanding in VLMs
paper_authors: Jianshu Zhang, Yijiang Li, Huifeixin Chen, Haoran Lu, Letian Xue
